messages:
alex: Quick sync — we need to lock down launch criteria and SLAs for the Private deployment wave that includes customer-managed networking. I sketched three rollout options and tradeoffs.
maya: thanks. can you paste the options?
alex: sure. Options:
- Option 1: Strict VPC-only GA. We require customers to hand over peering/VPC setup to us (fastest to guarantee latency/SLOs, but customer objections on network control).
- Option 2: Customer-managed networking GA with a defined handshake contract (customers manage routing/NAT, we provide clear TCP/port+ip handshake + health-check endpoints). More customer-friendly but more complex to validate.
- Option 3: Hybrid GA with an "edge fallback" mode — if customer's networking fails, we optionally route via Redwood-managed edge at higher cost and reduced feature set.
devon: +1 for Option 2 as a long-term target. But productizing the handshake contract requires changes to the installer and agent restart semantics. Current installer assumes outbound-only egress on ports 443, 3000 for control plane.
sree: infra note: we can implement a two-phase handshake (controlplane -> agent registration -> reverse-health check) that tolerates transient network flaps. That gives us canary-safe upgrades. But it adds ~2–3 work-weeks for rework of agent state machine and the installer docs.
carla: customer asks we logged last week: they will not allow any inbound ports to be opened on their side. They also want KMS integration for keys at rest and an audit trail for upgrade decisions. Is that compatible with Option 2? :thinking_face:
maya: yes, KMS is orthogonal. Agent can pick up keys from customer KMS (via vault/HSM) — need to list explicit env + permissions in the install guide. The bigger risk is inbound port constraints; we may need to rely entirely on outbound websocket/long-polling.
alex: good call. If we go outbound-only, handshake becomes: 1) agent starts outbound websocket to control plane 2) control plane verifies cert + model pin 3) agent accepts config and reports network topology. That should satisfy zero-inbound requirement.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: new note — current staging infra does not simulate flaky customer NAT. Please open ticket infra#1247 to add NAT/glare tests.
sree: added to infra backlog. We should also include a test harness that simulates MTU fragmentation, TCP resets, and long NAT timeouts.
devon: upgrade path question: can we guarantee zero-downtime upgrades if customers pin old model versions? We can if we support side-by-side agent processes and traffic drain. That requires packaging changes so agent can run v1 and v2 simultaneously during a rollout.
carla: timeline: customers expect a formal checklist and a migration window. They want a rollback playbook and SLA credits if upgrade causes >5m outage per tenant.
alex: proposed launch criteria for GA (draft):
- Installer supports outbound-only control-plane handshake
- Documented network contract + sample terraform for common cloud providers
- Canary upgrade path implemented (side-by-side agent + graceful drain)
- KMS/HSM key retrieval documented and verified in staging
- Integration tests for NAT/timeouts and rollback drills
- Customer acceptance test (CAT) template ready for first customers
maya: prioritization — we should split into 3 sprints: sprint A (handshake + installer changes), sprint B (upgrade side-by-side + tests), sprint C (docs + CAT + customer terraform). Delivery estimate: 8–10 weeks total if no major blockers.
sree: risk log:
- R1: customer's network idiosyncrasies (enterprise proxies, private DNS) — mitigation: sample configs + preflight network checker in installer.
- R2: latent bugs during side-by-side run causing double billing/duplicate tokens — mitigation: add idempotency token & leasing for runtime tokens.
- R3: audit/compliance gaps for on-prem data plane — mitigation: require audit logs and KMS integration before GA for regulated customers.
devon: small config snippet for outbound-only handshake (we can surface in docs):
```
# agent.yaml
control_plane:
  endpoint: wss://control.redwood.example
  proxy: http://proxy.corp.local:3128  # optional
  keepalive: 30s
ports: []  # empty = no inbound
```
carla: customers will ask about SLA numbers. What are we comfortable promising for GA? 99.0%? 99.5%?
alex: conservative ask: 99.0% per-tenant uptime for control-plane connectivity during GA. We can tighten to 99.5% after 2 quarters of telemetry. Must include explicit exclusions for customer-managed network outages.
maya: +1 on conservative. Also call out max RTO for upgrades: 5 minutes for routine patch; 30 minutes for major-version migrations (with CATs and scheduled windows).
sree: operational playbook items — we need automated fallback (edge routing) in the platform. That can be an optional feature flagged behind enterprise plan. If enabled, platform can route via managed edge when the customer's agent loses control-plane for >30s.
alex: action items:
- devon: prototype side-by-side agent packaging and deliver demo by EOW + update installer to support empty ports list (outbound-only). (owner: devon, due: 1773411200)
- sree: add NAT/flaky-network tests to staging harness and add infra#1247. (owner: sree, due: 1773497600)
- maya: draft customer network contract + terraform examples for AWS/GCP/Azure and a CAT template. (owner: maya, due: 1773584000)
- carla: draft SLA language + rollback credit formula and share with legal. (owner: carla, due: 1773660400)
devon: noted. one more ask — can we add a lightweight preflight that runs during install and outputs a single pass/fail JSON so sales/SEs can gate customers before engaging? should be quick to add.
maya: yes, include a preflight that checks outbound connectivity, DNS resolution to our endpoints, KMS reachability, and time skew. We'll capture the result in staging.
carla: I’ll loop in solutions engineering to validate the preflight for next-gen customers. Also, we should schedule a 30-minute customer-facing runbook review with the pilot customer next Wed.
alex: solid. final note: avoid any wording in the public docs that implies we manage customer networking — always use "customer-managed networking" and clearly list our fallback options and exclusions. I'll send a PR to the private deploy spec after sprint planning. :rocket:
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: reminder — meeting created: #private-deploy-sla-sync on 1773400000.
